text:
Maria: quick heads-up — after enabling continuous small-batch decoding smoothing in staging, we saw a weird latency spike on the decode hotpath for 1-4 token responses. attaching brief profiler output.
Raj: can you paste the top flamegraph snippet? is it the attention kernel or the KV cache churn?
Maria: looks like kernel selection flip is the trigger. when batch size estimator averages low, runtime picks FlashPaged variant -> higher kernel launch overhead on tiny sequences.
Tony: that makes sense. FlashPaged has more setup for page tables; on small decode batches fused/flash-unified might win.
Maria: exact numbers from a 1M-req synthetic run (staging, g4dn):
```
prefill path (baseline): 95 p95 latency
decode w/ continuous-smoothing: 138 p95 latency (+45%)
thruput: -9%
kernel selection: FlashPaged for seq<=32 by heuristic
kvcache evictions: +12% (frag)
```
Raj: hmm KV cache evictions up too — maybe the smoothing keeps more concurrent small decode inflight causing prefix KV fragmentation.
Lina: were there any changes to the kvcache eviction TTL or page-size recently?
Maria: no TTL changes. The smoothing changed micro-batch timing which increased interleaving of prefill vs decode streams; kvcache allocator is still LRU on page-chunks.
Alex: could be a collision between continuous-batching window (50ms) and our KVCACHE page-granularity (64KB). More tiny decodes means many short-lived entries, polluting LRU.
Raj: suggestion: add a decode-mode low-occupancy path that forces fused-smallkernel for estimated batch_size<=3 and seq<=16. Also consider a kvcache hotset pin for short-lived KV prefixes.
Tony: agree. We should also add a smoothing fallback: if selecting FlashPaged increases launch time > threshold, fall back to fused. We already sample both in nightly bench harness — just need to surfacing the signal to runtime.
Maria: perf-bot ran an automated A/B last night comparing three configs. results:
```
A: current-smoothing + FlashPaged default -> p95 138ms
B: smoothing + forced-fused-for-small -> p95 102ms
C: smoothing + FlashPaged + kvcache-hotset-pin -> p95 110ms
```
perf-bot: benchmark report uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/1816/continuous-smoothed-compare-2026-03-16.log
Lina: those deltas look convincing. B gets us close to baseline while keeping smoothing benefits for larger batches.
Raj: +1 to implement heuristic override. Also adding a cheap microprofile tag around kernel launch to collect statistical latency for each kernel_variant per request bucket.
Maria: I'll open a quick RFC with proposal: (1) runtime kernel override for small decode batches; (2) kvcache pinning for hot short prefixes; (3) microprofiler metric and alert when kernel switch increases p95 by >10% for 10m window.
Tony: timeline? we can land a toggle behind feature-flag this sprint.
Alex: I'll wire the perf dashboards to show kernel_variant by route so product teams can see impact (route-level p95 + kernel mix).
Maria: thanks all. for immediate triage I'm reverting smoothing default in staging and leaving the feature-flag on. will post RFC link here when created.
Raj: thanks — ping me on the RFC thread, I want to propose a simple cost model: launch_overhead - (batch_size*per_token_win) to pick kernel.
Maria: noted. small follow-up: anyone seen similar regression on A100? perf-bot only ran g4dn overnight.
Tony: no A100 run yet. I'll queue one with the same configs.
perf-bot: A100 run queued: job 2026-03-16-1816-a100
Alex: great, keep us posted. :thumbsup:
